title: Fermion Flavour Sector over Finite Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Substrate arithmetic: $\F_\Om$, the multiplicative cycle, the Frobenius $C_3$ Galois orbit, the quarter-turn $Q_4$, the admissible residue $\Om\equiv5\,(\mathrm{mod}\,12)$.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: One generation as the $\mathbf{16}$ of $\SO(10)$: field content, hypercharges, charges, anomaly freedom, $\sin^2\theta_W=3/8$, and the massless-photon / confining-gluon residues.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The Froggatt--Nielsen flavour mechanism and the Wolfenstein parametrisation.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The Gatto--Sartori--Tonin, Georgi--Jarlskog, and lopsided-$\SU(5)$ textures.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The seesaw mechanism and the renormalisation-group running.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Measured anchors: the two $\Delta m^2$, $M_R$, the charged-lepton and quark masses, $V_{us}$ and the mixing angles; the Koide identity is P1's prediction, not an input.

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: Matter is the circulant amplitude matrix $\sqrt M$; a mass is the squared modulus of a generation amplitude (the Born square). Falsifier: a charged-lepton spectrum departing from the circulant Koide form at improved precision (present agreement $6\times10^{-6}$).

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The three generations are the Frobenius $C_3$ Galois orbit: identical in every gauge number, differing only in mass. Falsifier: a fourth generation, or two generations differing in any gauge number.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The role depths $(0,1,2)$ of the closed ladder are the Froggatt--Nielsen flavour charges. Falsifier: a confirmed departure of the Wolfenstein hierarchy from the depth ladder $(0,1,2)$, e.g.\ $V_{us}$ outside the band of the Gatto relation for every phase $\varphi$.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The colour excess of the quark amplitudes is the Georgi--Jarlskog Clebsch $\Nc=3$; the squared amplitude is the cyclotomic norm $N(1-\zeta_n)$. Falsifier: a quark-to-lepton amplitude ratio departing from the $\Nc=3$ Clebsch at improved precision.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: A colourless sector (charged leptons, neutrinos) carries the undressed quarter-turn amplitude $r=\sqrt2$, i.e.\ $Q=2/3$. Falsifier: $Q_\ell\neq2/3$ at improved charged-lepton precision; for neutrinos, inverted ordering, a degenerate spectrum, or $\sum m_\nu\gtrsim120$\,meV.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: Generation universality $\Rightarrow$ the amplitude matrix is a $C_3$-circulant $\Rightarrow$ the Koide functional form.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: $Q=2/3\Leftrightarrow r=\sqrt2\Leftrightarrow\rho^2=\tfrac12$ (the equivalence an identity); the value $\rho^2=\tfrac12$ is the realisation B5.

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The leading boundary phase is the framed-rational winding $\delta_{\mathrm{LO}}=\tfrac38-\tfrac13=\tfrac1{24}$ cycle (split-torus boundary $\tfrac38$ minus generation $\tfrac13$; continuum $\pi/12$ [approx]); massless lightest generation.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: The squared amplitudes are the cyclotomic norms $r_\ell^2=N(1-i)=2$, $r_u^2=N(1-\omega)=3$ (on B5), hence $Q_\ell=\tfrac23$, $Q_u=\tfrac56$ in framed arithmetic ($Q_u=0.849$ in the working scheme, band $0.83$--$0.89$); the down sector is the GJ-dressed intermediate.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The cross-sector phase lock $\delta_\ell:\delta_d:\delta_u=1:\tfrac12:\tfrac13$ in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ working scheme of Table~\ref{tab:sectors} ($0.388$ for the up ratio with the pole charm mass).

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: The Gatto Cabibbo relation $V_{us}=|\sqrt{m_d/m_s}-e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{m_u/m_c}|$, the phase $\varphi$ a kernel datum ($85^\circ\pm10^\circ$ from the data).

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: Up-sector doubling $m^u_i\sim(m^d_i)^2$ from the $\mathbf{10}\cdot\mathbf{10}$ Yukawa.

rows.label: C8
rows.predicate: Lopsided $M_e=M_d^{\mathsf T}$ splits CKM (small) from PMNS (large); the CKM angle values reduce to the winding kernel and the shared $\sigma$.

rows.label: C9
rows.predicate: The reactor angle at leading order, $\sin\theta_{13}=\sin\theta_C/\sqrt2\simeq\delta_0/\sqrt2$ (quark--lepton complementarity): $0.159$ against the measured $0.149$, $7\%$, no correction derived.

rows.label: C10
rows.predicate: TM2 selected: the trivial $C_3$ character $(1,1,1)/\sqrt3$ is the protected column, so $\cos\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$ is locked to $\theta_{23}$ by \eqref{eq:tm2}; the magic Jarlskog $J=1/(6\sqrt3)$ is maximal CP, the sign fixed by the drive.

rows.label: C11
rows.predicate: Seesaw of circulants $\Rightarrow$ Koide-form (theorem); with $M_R\propto m_D$ ($\overline{\mathbf{126}}$ alignment, a realisation) the seesaw gives $m_\nu=m_D^{\mathsf T}$, $r_\nu=\sqrt2$ (transpose fixed point).

rows.label: C11b
rows.predicate: Drive-invariant boundary branch: the lightest colourless neutrino sits at the quarter-turn zero (as the electron), selecting the normal near-$m_1{=}0$ branch; the signed $r_\nu=\sqrt2$ circulant solves both orderings exactly, so the branch is the sole ordering assumption. Falsifier: inverted ordering.

rows.label: C12
rows.predicate: The generation $\mathbf{16}$ is the four-chart reflection algebra $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^4)\cong\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(\C^5)$, the quarter-turn the fifth direction; projection anchored at $\nu^c=\Lambda^0$.

blocks.title: What the construction explains: the surplus over the flavour data

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Koide ratio} is exactly $2/3$ given the quarter-turn realisation B5, the cube-root generation orbit bisected at the quarter-turn ($\rho^2=2^{-1}$), an exact value rather than an unexplained empirical coincidence.

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The up-quark Koide value} is $5/6$ in framed arithmetic ($0.849$ in the working scheme, $0.832$ with pole masses), the cube-root colour norm $r_u^2=N(1-\omega)=3$ against the colourless $N(1-i)=2$, a ratio where the Standard Model carries no relation at all.

rows.label: X3
rows.predicate: \textbf{The flavour charges} are the role depths $(0,1,2)$ of the closed primitive-role ladder, derived as the three generative roles rather than assigned to fit the hierarchy.

rows.label: X4
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Cabibbo angle} is the Gatto relation $V_{us}=|\sqrt{m_d/m_s}-e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{m_u/m_c}|$ following from the role-depth texture, the leading term at $0.3\%$ and the phase $\varphi$ a kernel datum, so two otherwise-independent observables are tied rather than measured apart.

rows.label: X5
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Georgi--Jarlskog factor} is the colour count $N_c=3$, the $B\!-\!L$ Clebsch of the $\overline{\mathbf{126}}$, not a texture coefficient inserted by hand; its double ratio $9$ against the measured $10.4\pm0.5$ is the open $15\%$ excess of the minimal Clebsch.

rows.label: X6
rows.predicate: \textbf{The up-sector doubling} $m^u_i\sim(m^d_i)^2$ is forced by the $\mathbf{10}\cdot\mathbf{10}$ Yukawa, so the steeper up hierarchy is a consequence rather than a separate assumption.

rows.label: X7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The electron's extreme lightness} is the quarter-turn boundary: the lightest generation sits where the winding amplitude vanishes, massless at leading order, rather than an anomalously small Yukawa tuned by hand.

rows.label: X8
rows.predicate: \textbf{The large-lepton, small-quark mixing split} is the lopsided $M_e=M_d^{\mathsf T}$: one off-diagonal feeds the invisible right-handed quark rotation and, transposed, the visible left-handed lepton rotation, so the two mixing matrices are one structure rather than two unrelated ones.

rows.label: X9
rows.predicate: \textbf{The reactor angle} is, at leading order, $\sin\theta_{13}=\sin\theta_C/\sqrt2=0.159$, quark--lepton complementarity through the quarter-turn, $7\%$ above the observed $0.149$ with no correction derived: a leading-order estimate of the mixing parameter, not a prediction.

rows.label: X10
rows.predicate: \textbf{Near-maximal leptonic CP} is the cube-root phase: $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega=\sqrt3/2$ gives the maximal Jarlskog $J=1/(6\sqrt3)$, so the cubic reappears as CP violation rather than a free phase fitted to data.

rows.label: X11
rows.predicate: \textbf{The neutrino spectrum} (a near-massless lightest state, $\sum m_\nu\simeq59\,$meV on the normal branch) follows from colourlessness fixing $Q_\nu=2/3$, the transpose fixed point $M_R\propto m_D$ and the boundary-branch realisation that selects the ordering, rather than three independent neutrino masses.

rows.label: P1
rows.predicate: Charged-lepton Koide $Q_\ell=2/3$ exact on B5 (measured $0.666661\pm0.000007$); $m_e=0.5106$ vs $0.5110$ MeV. Falsifier: a lepton-mass shift of $Q_\ell$ off $2/3$ beyond the $\tau$-mass tolerance.

rows.label: P2
rows.predicate: Up-quark Koide $Q_u=5/6$ in framed arithmetic, $r_u^2=N(1-\omega)=3$; continuum $0.849$ in the working scheme, $0.832$ with pole masses, band $0.83$--$0.89$. Falsifier: up/charm/top masses moving $Q_u$ outside the band in every standard scheme.

rows.label: P3
rows.predicate: Cabibbo $V_{us}=|\sqrt{m_d/m_s}-e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{m_u/m_c}|$: leading term $0.224^{+0.011}_{-0.004}$ vs $0.2243$ ($0.3\%$), the up term $\pm0.04$ with $\varphi$ open. Falsifier: no $\varphi$ satisfying the relation within the input band.

rows.label: P5
rows.predicate: Normal neutrino ordering, from $Q_\nu=2/3$, the two $\Delta m^2$ and the boundary branch (C11b); the signed circulant solves both orderings. Falsifier: inverted ordering.

rows.label: P6
rows.predicate: Mass-sum floor $\sum m_\nu=58.7$ meV ($m_1{\simeq}0$, $m_2{\simeq}8.6$, $m_3{\simeq}50$ meV; $58.8$ at NuFIT~6.0), the $m_1=0$ normal-ordering floor. Falsifier: a cosmological $\sum m_\nu<0.058$ eV.

rows.label: P7
rows.predicate: Effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}{\simeq}1.5$--$3.7$ meV (NO, $m_1{\simeq}0$, circulant phase). Falsifier: a $0\nu\beta\beta$ signal at the inverted scale $15$--$50$ meV.

rows.label: P8
rows.predicate: Leptonic CP locked to the octant by \eqref{eq:tm2}: $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}\in(204^\circ,310^\circ)$ over the $3\sigma$ $\theta_{23}$ range, $\pm124^\circ$/$\pm74^\circ$ at the NuFIT~6.0 best fits, $\sin\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}{<}0$, $J=1/(6\sqrt3)$. Falsifier: CP-conserving $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$, $\sin\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}{>}0$, or $(\theta_{23},\delta_{\mathrm{CP}})$ off the relation.

rows.label: V1
rows.predicate: The validation package \texttt{finite-ring-space/src/28-flavour}: the sixteen scripts as written --- \src{flv.\allowbreak exact\_\allowbreak core}, \src{flv.\allowbreak framed\_\allowbreak koide}, \src{flv.tier\_b}, \src{flv.m10}, \src{flv.delta}, \src{flv.\allowbreak revision\_\allowbreak checks}, \src{flv.\allowbreak quark\_\allowbreak amp}, \src{flv.\allowbreak up\_\allowbreak doubling}, \src{flv.spurion}, \src{flv.theta13}, \src{flv.neutrino}, \src{flv.pmns\_cp}, \src{flv.\allowbreak tm2\_\allowbreak jointfit}, \src{flv.scale\_a}, \src{flv.\allowbreak coupling\_\allowbreak anchor}, \src{flv.\allowbreak alpha\_\allowbreak probe} --- run through one registry, one family per script, its micro-checks the script's own verdict lines together with the registry's predicates on the script's namespace and output (four scripts print without asserting; every headline numeral is pinned by a labelled check in \texttt{flvcommon.py}), each family naming the rows it witnesses; the notebook \texttt{28-flavour-main.ipynb} executes them in the browser and the driver \texttt{run\_all.py} writes \texttt{results.json}.

rows.label: V2
rows.predicate: The discipline, recorded per family as its class: \textsf{EXACT} --- integer, $\F_p$, $\F_{p^2}$ or cyclotomic arithmetic throughout, no float in any asserted claim (\src{flv.\allowbreak exact\_\allowbreak core}, \src{flv.\allowbreak framed\_\allowbreak koide}, the load-bearing identities of the mass sector); \textsf{MIXED} --- an own exact check for at least one claim, the continuum confined to labelled [approx] comparisons (seven families); \textsf{APPROX} --- continuum or numerical by construction, a numerical reconfirmation of an identity proven exactly in \src{flv.\allowbreak exact\_\allowbreak core}, a comparison with measured data, or an $\Om$-hard reading (seven families).

rows.label: V3
rows.predicate: What the run does not decide: the $\Om$-hard residues (Z1--Z4) enter only as labelled readings (the transmutation exponent, the coupling anchor, the one-loop fermion sum, $\delta_0=Q/3$ as a confrontation); the joint mixing fit of \src{flv.\allowbreak tm2\_\allowbreak jointfit} is status, not a test (five parameters for four observables); the reactor angle is a leading-order estimate at $7\,\%$ (C9), not a prediction; the Georgi--Jarlskog double ratio is carried as the open $15\,\%$ excess; five of the scripts' own checks are statements, not decisions, and are recorded as such in the package README.

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: The lepton winding phase $\delta_0$: the one $\Om$-hard drive-orientation residue. Neither a geometric nor a profinite derivation fixes it, the drive-orientation Gauss sum equidistributing. Sub-horizon reading $\delta_0=Q/3=2/9$ ($3\delta_0=Q$); leading $\delta_{\mathrm{LO}}=\tfrac38-\tfrac13$ framed-rational (C3); phase residue carried by $\mathrm{Re}(b^{3})$.

rows.label: Z2
rows.predicate: The quark phases $\delta_d=\delta_0/2$, $\delta_u=\delta_0/3$ locked to $\delta_0$ (C5); the neutrino phase $\delta_\nu\simeq0.48$, which the seesaw resets, and the quark CP phase are independent $\Om$-hard residues.

rows.label: Z3
rows.predicate: The absolute masses and the electroweak scale $v$: $\Om$-hard, the matter face of the scale operator (master ledger Z6).

rows.label: Z4
rows.predicate: $\alpha^{-1}(0)$: the electromagnetic face of the scale operator, $\Om$-hard (master ledger Z8).

legend.name: Import
legend.text: A standard result or measured datum used here without reproof.

legend.name: Realisation
legend.text: A forced identification of a physical term with the substrate object it denotes: constitutive, not interpretive; defended by the totality of consequences registered under it; killed by the falsifier stated in its row.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Derived within this paper from the rows above it; where a family identifier is named, its content is verified by the validation package.

legend.name: Theorem on a realisation
legend.text: A theorem consumed through a declared realisation: in block P the paper's predictions, each derived and witnessed, stated with its falsifier and its present confrontation; a refuted confrontation fires the realisation's falsifier, not the theorem.

legend.name: $\Om$-hard
legend.text: Decided by the totality; not closeable by a bounded observer.
